pie.line: Still warm. The crust cracked a bit on one side and that is how you know a person made it.

jam.line: Sealed while hot. It will keep long past the season it came out of.

cordial.line: A splash in cold water on a bad day. Sweet, and sharper than you expect.

bouquet.line: Cut on a slant and tied with twine, the way you do when you mean it.

wreath.line: Wound onto a willow ring. Hang it on a door and the door is somebody's.

bundle.line: Hung upside down from the beam. The whole kitchen smells of it for a week.

shepherds pie.line: More gravy than not, mash crisped on top. Rowan's, and he will tell you so.

tincture.line: Steeped dark in a small brown bottle. Closest thing this house has to a potion.

smoked fish.line: Hung over apple wood with the window cracked so the whole house smells of it for a day and a half.

fish stew.line: On the back of the stove since noon. Better tomorrow, which is the entire point of a stew.

fish on the fire.line: Split, salted, laid on a flat stone in the embers on the bank. Eaten with your fingers about nine feet from where it was caught.

a cairn.line: Three river stones balanced on the bank, biggest first. It means somebody was here and went home safe. Leave it standing.

keepsake.line: One found thing and one flower, pressed flat together between two heavy books. It costs almost nothing to make, which is the point: you can always afford to make somebody one.

charm.makes: a charm of small found things
charm.line: Threaded onto a length of waxed cord, in the order they were picked up rather than the order that looks best. Nothing here was bought. A bird brought every piece of it indoors.

mobile.line: Balanced on two crossed dowels until it stopped tipping, which took longer than making it. It turns slowly in a draught nobody can feel and throws small pieces of light around the room.

planted boot.makes: {crop} growing out of an old boot
planted boot.line: Drainage holes were already generously provided. It sits by the step looking pleased with itself, which is more than the boot ever managed on a foot.

sleep sachet.line: A little cloth square, stitched shut and slipped under the pillow. Crush it once with your thumb before you lie down.

mushrooms on toast.line: Butter, too much of it, and the pan still hissing when it comes to the table.

roasted nuts.line: Shells cracked by the fire. Warm in the hand long after they leave the oven.

venison stew.line: Dark stock, roots cut thick, and the meat given the whole afternoon. Nothing from the hunt is wasted.

game pie.line: Pepper in the gravy and a thumbprint at the edge of the crust. Made to come home to.

vegetable stew.makes: a pot of garden vegetable stew
vegetable stew.line: Beans, bright vegetables and roots cut thick, with a handful of herbs. Enough to bring a few friends to the table.

garden salad.line: Fresh picked, roughly chopped, and tossed with fragrant leaves. A cool bowl to carry out into the sun.

herbed vegetables.line: Edges browned, herbs caught in the warm oil, and one piece stolen straight from the tray. Pack the rest for the path.

yew longbow.line: Worked until both limbs bend together. The string sits quiet against the bracer and the deep wood answers more cleanly.

antler-handled knife.line: Flint edge, antler grip, waxed cord. A working thing made beside the river from what the wood gave back.

quiet hide boots.makes: a pair of quiet hide boots
quiet hide boots.line: Soft-soled and rubbed with rosemary oil. They make less argument with dry leaves than bare feet do.

field cloak.line: Dark green under the trees, brown at the hem, broad enough to cover a basket when the rain comes sideways.

gathering satchel.line: A wide mouth, a split hazel frame, and one pressed flower under the flap. It finds room for the extra handful.
